metadata.notes: PR 3.4cd Cardinality specialist exercise. The constrained _fixture schema (single non-key source field 'name') doesn't support genuine many_to_one (which requires ≥ 2 contributing source fields). Within this constraint, the fixture uses business_context to describe a one_to_many split scenario: source 'name' contains a comma-separated full identifier whose first segment maps to target 'label'. The Cardinality specialist should classify this as a one-to-one mapping with a transformation_pattern of 'split_first_segment_on_comma' — NOT one_to_many (which would imply multiple targets). Phase 3.8 cohort eval will replace this with a multi-source-field fixture for genuine many_to_one testing. Score interpretation: 1.0 if the agent emits the mapping with appropriate transformation reasoning; partial credit if the cardinality is correct but transformation_pattern is missing.
metadata.business_context: The source 'name' field on fixture_source_table stores comma-separated values in the format 'full_identifier,internal_code,version_tag' (e.g., 'customer-alpha-123,INT-001,v1'). The target 'label' field on fixture_target_table expects ONLY the first segment (the full_identifier portion). A transformation is required: split the source 'name' value on the first comma and take the leading segment. This is a one-to-one mapping with a split-and-take-first transformation pattern, NOT a many_to_one (no other source fields contribute) and NOT a one_to_many (only ONE target field receives a derived value).
